steps.title: Set Your Market And Video Language
steps.text: In Settings → Profile → 1 · Content Preferences, enter your city, state, and video language. This powers live local market research, trending topics, and auto-localized templates.

steps.title: Create Your AI Voice
steps.text:
In Settings → Profile → 2 · AI Voice Clone, record or upload about 30 seconds of your voice. Your AI videos will speak in your voice.
The card has two tabs. Record my voice gives you a short script to read aloud, which you can edit or replace with your own words. Press Start recording, speak clearly and naturally for at least 30 seconds, press Stop Recording, then Use this recording, or Re-record to try again. Upload a file is for a recording you already have.
If your voice clone ever stops being available, a video tells you before it is made and nothing is taken from your plan. Record your voice again here and try again.

steps.title: Complete Your Brand Profile
steps.text: In Settings → Profile → 3 · Brand & AI Profile, add your name, brokerage, phones, website, and license number. Upload your logo and your headshot — the headshot becomes your AI Photo Avatar, and your contact card and logo appear automatically in every video.

steps.title: Make Your Digital Twin (Optional)
steps.text:
Your Digital Twin is a lifelike video of you that talks and moves like you. In Settings → Profile → 4 · Digital Twin (inside Brand & AI Profile), record about 2 minutes of yourself talking to the camera: phone at eye level, good light, quiet room, only you in the shot. Upload it or pick a recording from the Camera tab, then tap Train Digital Twin. It's ready in 15 to 30 minutes, and it shows up as an avatar look in every video. On the free plan your twin appears in Avatar (You) in circle; on paid plans it works in Avatar (You in full) video too. A vertical video shows you in the room you filmed in. Your twin needs your approval once, right after it's trained: Settings shows Approval Required. Press Approve My Digital Twin, follow the short approval on camera, and you come back to SparkReels with it marked approved (if not, press I've approved it ). Until then it can't be used in a video; if you try, the video setup offers Approve now and nothing is charged. In Avatar in circle, the circle follows you as you move. You can delete your twin any time in Settings.
Backgrounds for your Agent Intro
Your twin is filmed upright, so in your horizontal Agent Intro your own background is taken away and you stand full size in front of a new one. In Settings → 4 · Digital Twin, Your backgrounds keeps them: a color, a town photo, or press + Describe, type or say a place and press Make it (about 20 seconds). Tap one to make it your default. Up to 20 new backgrounds a month. Avatar video with your twin is made by our video agent, which sets its own scenes, so it doesn't use these.
Outfits for your twin
Want your twin in something else? In Settings → 4 · Digital Twin, under Outfits, describe it (like navy blazer over a white shirt ) and press New outfit. It takes a minute or two, and it moves like your twin. Each outfit then shows up as a look in video setup and works everywhere your twin does, approval and backgrounds included. Your first new look each month is free; after that each one uses one short video. Tap the bin on an outfit to remove it. The New look under your photo avatar changes only the photo avatar, not your twin.

steps.title: Set Your Default Video CTA
steps.text: In Settings → Profile → 5 · Default Video CTA, add your years in real estate and review the pre-written closing call-to-action. It auto-fills your name, team, and each video's city — edit it once and every video ends with a proven subscribe-and-contact close. Change it later and it carries into videos you have already started, unless you typed over the closing line in that video; Use my saved CTA there brings it back. Keep it to 40 words (about 17 seconds): the count under the box shows yours with your details filled in, because it's spoken inside your 2-minute video.

steps.title: Save Your Import Address
steps.text:
In Settings → Profile → 6 · Import Articles By Email you have a private address that looks like yourname-k7m3qz@in.sparkreels.ai. Forward anything to it — a newsletter, a market report, an article someone sent you, or a post you wrote yourself — and it appears inside SparkReels within a minute, with the signatures, forwarding headers and unsubscribe footers already stripped out. Press Email this address to me and save it to your contacts; after that, forwarding is the whole of it.
It is private to your account, so treat it like a password. Anyone who has it can send articles into your list, and you can replace it any time from the same screen.
Once something has arrived, Spark Studio has it under My Content/Forwarded in, in the Script source row, with a new badge when something has come in since you last looked. Open it, choose From email, and pick the one you want. Nothing is written until you press the button at the bottom of the page. The whole piece is read, up to about 10,000 words, so a long market report is used to its last page. Forwarded emails are kept for 30 days.
On a paid plan, each email you forward also becomes a video draft on the AutoSparks page, ready to approve (step 16).

steps.title: Put SparkReels On Your Phone
steps.text:
Settings → Profile → 7 · Put SparkReels on your phone shows how to open SparkReels like an app, one tap from your Home Screen.
iPhone: open sparkreels.ai in Safari, tap Share (the square with an arrow), then Add to Home Screen. Android: open it in Chrome, tap the ⋮ menu, then Add to Home screen (or Install app ). On a phone that can install it straight away, the card has a button for it.

steps.title: Connect Your CRM
steps.text:
Settings → Profile → 8 · CRM Integration sends your work to the CRM you already use.
BoldTrail. If you use BoldTrail, SparkReels can email your sellers and clients through it, from your own BoldTrail address, and BoldTrail keeps each email on that contact's record. In BoldTrail, go to Lead Engine → Lead Dropbox → My API Tokens, tick Contacts, press Generate and copy the token. Then paste it into the BoldTrail box in Settings → 8 · CRM Integration and press Connect. It's saved securely and shown only by its last four characters; Disconnect removes it. If BoldTrail won't send with a Contacts token, make one with All ticked. Tokens last a year.
GoHighLevel and other CRMs. Every video you finish can be sent to your CRM automatically, with its title, a short caption, the link, the thumbnail and your name, so a workflow there can text it, email it or post it for you. In GoHighLevel, create a workflow with an Inbound Webhook trigger and copy its address. In SparkReels press Set up for GoHighLevel, paste the address, keep Video published ticked and save. Test sends a sample with the same fields a real video has, so GoHighLevel can learn them. Want it done for you? Press Ask for the workflow on the GoHighLevel card and we'll email you a ready-made one with step-by-step instructions. Any tool that takes a webhook (Zapier, Make and others) works the same way.

steps.title: Your Account
steps.text: Settings → Profile → 9 · Account is where you set or change your password (if you signed in with Google, you can add one here), sign out, or delete your account.

steps.title: Connect YouTube And Your Other Accounts
steps.text:
In Settings → 10 · Social Accounts, connect the Google account that owns your channel. One-time tip: verify the channel by phone at youtube.com/verify so your thumbnails are added automatically.
Still not working? YouTube's verify page opens for whichever channel your browser is on, so check the picture at its top right is this channel. If it isn't, open the page in a private window signed in to this channel only. And one phone number verifies two channels a year: if YouTube says yours is used up, use another phone or a landline.
Thumbnail didn't go up? Your video still posted. YouTube only takes a custom thumbnail from a phone-verified channel. Verify the channel at youtube.com/verify, then open the video's Publish window in My Sparks and press Update it on YouTube under the thumbnail. Or download the thumbnail there and add it in YouTube Studio.
On a paid plan the same screen has More platforms: Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn, TikTok, X, Threads and Google Business. Press Connect beside each one you use and approve it on that platform's own screen, which names Upload-Post, the service that delivers your posts. Connect as many as you like, and Disconnect any of them there too. A few need the right kind of account: Instagram must be a Business or Creator account linked to a Facebook Page, Facebook must be a Page rather than your personal profile, and Google Business must be a verified profile.
If an account can post to more than one place, a Posts to choice appears under it: which Facebook Page, your LinkedIn profile or a company page, which Google Business location. Pick once and every post goes there. With two Facebook Pages or two locations you do have to pick, or posts there won't go out.

steps.title: Your Plan And Buying More Videos
steps.text:
Settings → 11 · Billing & Plan shows your plan, when it renews, and what you have left this month.
Every plan includes 4 short videos a month; Producer adds 2 long videos and Influencer 4. They reset each billing month. Blog posts, camera recordings and AutoSparks drafts don't use any. Need more? Buy More Videos adds one short video for $25 or one long video for $29, and bought videos never expire; your plan's videos are used first. The AutoSparks page shows Videos left this month, and a draft you have no video left for says Needs 1 more video: pressing Approve on it offers to upgrade or buy one.
Manage Billing changes your plan or card, or cancels. A cancelled plan stays active until the end of the month you paid for.

steps.title: Start With The Topic, Then Choose What To Make
steps.text:
Spark Studio has two sections, then More options. 1 · Topic — one card with the mic and a box, Tell Sparklee what to make, where you say or type what it's about (step 13). Under it, Not sure what to make? Tap an idea shows four ideas with your town filled in; See all ideas opens the full list. 2 · Create — four cards: Video / Reel, Camera/Teleprompter, Blog or Listings & photos. Video / Reel stays on this page; the other three each open a page of their own, with Back on the bar at the bottom to return here. A topic you already said or typed comes with you. More options folds the rest away until you want it: 3 · Script Source — AI writes it from a topic, or My Content/Forwarded in, which is also where anything you forwarded in turns up (step 6). A listing or a photos only reel skips this one (step 19). 4 · Details — the city and state, who it's for, and a video's format. Details opens by itself when your city and state are missing, since Next needs them.
You don't have to work down all four. Give it a topic at the top, check the city and state, and press Next at the bottom. The sections underneath are there for when you want to change something first.
Video / Reel is three kinds of video, and they sit right under that card for you to pick, so the script is written to suit. Pick one any time; if you press Next first, they light up and ask. Avatar video puts you on screen with b-roll and graphics made for you. Avatar in circle puts you in a corner circle over scenes that follow what you're saying. Voice over only has nobody on screen: it is a Scenes Reel (step 17). Each uses one short video. If your sentence already said which, such as “with my avatar” or “voice over only”, it isn't asked.
Whatever you pick, it starts a Spark — the folder holding that topic's script, its videos, its article and where they've been published. It's created the moment you begin, so an idea saved and left half-finished is still there marked Draft, not lost. Part 5 explains where Sparks live and how they differ from the videos themselves.
Already written it? My Content/Forwarded in is the one place for it, the second box under Script source. Paste your words in, or attach a PDF, a link, or an email you forwarded to your import address (step 6). On a video you then say what happens to them: Speak it word for word, for a finished script, or Have AI write from it, which either writes a new script from it or shortens an article of your own. To write a new one, press Write my script from the link (or the PDF or email); type something in Anything to focus on? first if you want it to lean one way. The script comes back for you to read before anything is made. + Opening line under it adds a line spoken first, which also becomes the video's title. If an email's subject names a town, the city and state fill in for you. Recording yourself has its own version of this, From a document.
On the Blog page the same tile is there, and you choose what happens to it: Use it as it is, which publishes your words unchanged and takes seconds, or Write a new article from it, which covers the same ground in your voice for your market. Use the first for your own writing and the second for someone else's — a newsletter another person wrote is theirs, not yours to publish. A market report is the second kind: it is a data provider's pages of listings, so have a new article written from it rather than publishing it as it stands.
Who is it for? Audience, Tone and Why are three optional pickers under Details. What you choose shapes the script, the article and the Spark Tools afterwards. You can also just say them: “for first-time buyers”, “make it vertical”. If your audience is not on the list — first responders, nurses relocating — choose Add your own… at the bottom of Audience and type it. It is saved to your account, so it is there on your phone and your computer, and choosing it again shows Remove from my list for when you no longer want it.

steps.title: Speak It Or Type It — Your Choice
steps.text:
Need help on a section? Tap Ask Sparklee, the gold star just under the top bar on the right of every page, and ask out loud how to do something. She answers in a few seconds, out loud and on screen, from this guide. Each conversation runs up to five minutes. Five conversations a day before you pick a plan, twenty a day on one. The Topic card at the top of Spark Studio reads Tell Sparklee what to make. It has one mic and one box, and they are the same thing: what you say shows up in the box, and what you type goes in the same place. Tap the mic and say the whole thing in one sentence — “Create a blog for downsizers about one-floor living in Springfield” or “Make a vertical video with my avatar about the Riverside market” — and tap the mic again when you're done. Your words stay in the box, so a misheard town or street name is a quick fix.
A moment after you stop, the page fills itself in from what you said: the card under 2 · Create lights up, the city and state appear under 4 · Details, and the audience and format are set if you named them. Look down the page to check it, change anything by hand, and press Next at the bottom. Say more and it is added to the box and read again. Say “Spark it” and it presses Next for you.
Sparklee, make it (paid plans), the button under the box, has Sparklee do the whole video herself. Say it all at once, for example “Make a market update for Springfield this week, horizontal, my twin, post it Friday”. She asks only for what's missing (the topic, or the town). Then she writes the script, blog, title and thumbnail and makes the video, which takes about 10 to 12 minutes. It comes back as a card under the box, and on AutoSparks under From Sparklee: Watch, Edit thumbnail, Edit title and caption, then Approve to post. Nothing posts until you approve it. It posts to the accounts you used last time, on the day you said (or the next day), at your Halo time. Don't post it yourself as well. On the free plan, or for a blog or a camera take, she fills the page in instead and you press Next.
A blog is written straight away. A video stops at its script, so nothing comes out of your plan until you choose to make it. The script's length follows the format: up to 90 seconds for Vertical, up to 2 minutes for Horizontal, and up to 8 minutes for Longform.
Say “make a reel about…” and it makes a Voice over only Scenes Reel (step 17). Say who's in it, as in “a reel with my avatar”, and it makes that instead.
The cards follow along. Say “create a blog” and the Blog card is the one picked; tap a card yourself and the box makes that instead.
You can start from an email you forwarded the same way: “Create a blog from my Springfield market report email.” It only looks through your emails when you say “email” or “forwarded”, so “a market update for Springfield” still means a fresh one.
You don't have to say it all at once. Give it the topic, then the town, then who it's for, one answer at a time, and it keeps what it has already heard. On a desktop you can hold Spacebar anywhere on the page instead of tapping the mic. Once it says it has everything, saying “Spark it” starts it too.
Prefer typing, or want a suggestion instead of a blank box? The box shows a Try example that changes every few seconds; press the empty box to use the one showing, or just start typing. Under it is a Quick win: a ready topic for your town in one press, with a new idea each time you sign in (your very first one is a market update). Then What buyers ask AI (step 25), and under that Or try: ideas with your city filled in, with More ideas opening the whole list and a search box. Tap one and it lands in the same box the mic writes into, so you can add to it before you send. The first chip, 👋 Agent Intro, is a short video introducing you: your name, brokerage, area and years are filled in from Settings, you pick who you help most and add anything personal or your profile link. It runs about 30 seconds. You get the intro script plus a short and a long bio in the Share Kit. It's you, full screen, and with your Digital Twin it's made on our most lifelike avatar. Producer and Influencer get one free every month; otherwise it uses 1 short video (on the free plan, your free video). Either way, AI researches live market data for your city and writes a broadcast-quality script with real stats.

steps.title: Review & Edit The Script
steps.text:
Pick your favorite hook — it becomes the video title too, so the two never disagree. Edit the script freely; a live word counter keeps you inside the cap. Your Call To Action is on the next screen, in Video setup under Music: it is spoken after your script, so edit it there, or tick No call to action to end the video on your script. Regenerate redoes it from the same topic — it asks first, since it discards your edits.
Listen reads your script aloud in your own cloned voice, so you hear how the video will sound before you make it. Listen to the article does the same for the blog post in your Share Kit, and each AutoSparks draft has Listen too. The first time takes a few seconds for a script, up to about a minute for a long article; after that it plays at once. Pause or stop any time. With no voice clone yet, it reads in a standard voice.

steps.title: Choose Format And Who's On Screen — Then Generate
steps.text:
Pick a format: Vertical 9:16 for Reels, Shorts and TikTok, or Horizontal 16:9 for YouTube and websites — both up to 2 minutes — or Longform 16:9 (up to 8 minutes. Add your own photos and you're in a circle over them; add none and you're full screen the whole time. Long videos have their own monthly allowance — 2 with Producer, 4 with Influencer — or $29 on its own.)
Then who's on screen, four choices that are the same for every script, whether AI wrote it or you pasted your own:
Avatar video — you on screen, with b-roll and graphics made for you. Up to 2 minutes, so it is not offered for Longform. It takes a script of up to 290 words, counting your closing line. If yours is longer, Avatar video is greyed out and a note under the choices says how many words you have. Press Shorten to fit and the script is cut to fit, or Shorten closing line to trim your closing line yourself. With your Digital Twin it is a full Avatar video too, vertical or horizontal.
Avatar in circle — you in a corner circle, speaking the script exactly as written, over scenes made for each sentence. Attach a few photos and each takes a sentence among the scenes; attach many and the photos are the background. Up to 12 of your photos move gently, a slow drift made from the photo itself and checked to stay true to it; the description then says “Photos animated with AI.” On a listing video, Open with me in front of the home starts it with a 6-second shot of you at the front of the listing, made with AI from your look and its front photo: choose Full body, Chest up or Off. The last 5 seconds show your contact card beside your circle: your logo, name, company, phone and website, from your profile.
Voice over only — nobody on screen. Your voice over AI scenes made for each sentence, or over your photos if you attached some. The quickest of the three.
You on camera — the free way out of this screen. It hands your script and photos to the camera instead of making a video.
The first three use one video from your plan. Attach photos or documents as b-roll, and hit Spark Video. How long it takes follows the length of the script, not the format: Voice over only is usually ready in 2 to 10 minutes, an avatar video in about 10 to 12, and a long one can take up to an hour. You can close the page: when it's done, Sparklee pops up on whatever page you're on with Watch and Edit thumbnail, and if you've left the app you get a Your video is ready email instead.
Above the button, Ready to make checks your voice, that your look fits the video's shape, your Digital Twin approval and your videos left. Anything not ready has a button that fixes it ( Approve now, Use the wide one, Get more ), and Spark Video stays off until it's all green, so nothing is charged for a video that can't be made. The look that fits the shape is picked for you; Change look shows them all. If a video fails, your allowance is refunded automatically. When lots of videos are being made at once, yours waits in line and starts on its own a few minutes later; nothing is charged until it starts.

steps.title: AutoSparks, Halo Sites And Email Drafts (Paid Plans)
steps.text:
Every Sunday evening, SparkReels writes 3 posts for your week about your market, the season, and what buyers are asking AI: 1 video and 2 blog posts to start, or pick your own mix at the top of the AutoSparks page (2 videos and 1 blog, 3 videos, or 3 blogs). Each video you approve uses one of your plan's videos for the month; the top of the page shows how many you have left. Every video also comes with its own blog article. Each comes with its script, blog post, title and description, set for Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday at 9 AM, or the 3 days and time you pick under Post on. On Monday morning you get an email: “Your week is ready.” Open AutoSparks in the menu and, on each one, press Approve to open it ready to make, Change to edit it first, or Skip. On a video, Record it myself opens the camera with the script in the teleprompter, free. Want something specific? Use Ask for ideas: type or say a topic, and up to 3 drafts are written in about a minute. Nothing is made, posted or charged until you approve it, and you can turn AutoSparks off at the top of that page.
Halo sites
If you have a Halo website, add it in Settings → Halo website, right after CRM Integration: press Add your Halo site, type the address, like springfieldhomes.com, and press Add. You can add more than one. Its drafts show up on the AutoSparks page. No Halo website yet? The same card has Get Halo, which opens Halo's sign-up ($99 a month, billed by Halo). Every morning SparkReels looks for what is new on them: new blog posts and guides, and your market report and events page when they change. Pages already on your site when you add it are left alone, so adding a site never turns your old posts into videos.
Choose which pages to make videos from under Videos from (Blog, Guides, Events, Market report and more), how many a month under Each month (1 to 4, one a week), and the day and time under Post on. The rest are the starting choices for every Halo video: Look (Avatar in circle, Avatar video, or Mix, which uses Avatar video for the market report and Avatar in circle for the rest), Avatar, Size, Post to (the accounts you connected), Captions and Music. When your sites publish more than your month holds, the others wait under Also new on your sites, and Use instead swaps one in.
Each Halo draft shows up under From your Halo sites with its thumbnail and setup at a glance, and a link to the post it came from. The script is written from the post itself. The thumbnail uses the post's photo, or an AI picture of the town when there isn't one, with your headshot on top. Press Setup to change anything for that one video: the picture (from the post, an AI picture, or Upload your own), look, avatar, size, what is on screen (stock clips of the area or the post's own photos), captions, music, accounts and when it posts. Edit script opens it in the editor.
Changing a draft without making two videos
Nothing is made until you press Make video, so change as much as you like first. The look, size, avatar, captions, music, picture, accounts or day: press Setup on the card. Changing these makes nothing.
The words: press Edit script, change the script, then press Save Draft next to the video settings. Don't press Spark Video there. Go back to AutoSparks; the card shows your new words.
When you're happy, press Make video on the card. It uses the card's Setup choices, not the editor's video settings, so change the look and size in Setup and only the words in the editor.
Pressed Spark Video in the editor by mistake? That's fine: the card then says Video made and shows Watch and Approve to post for that video, using nothing more. A draft never makes a second video.
Make it, watch it, then approve it Make video makes the video and uses one video from your plan. Nothing posts yet. The card says Making your video until it's done.
When it's done, the card shows Watch. Watch it first. Below it you can change Posts on (the day and time), press Edit thumbnail (background, words, font, size, style and colour, the same editor as in Publish), and press Edit title and caption to change the YouTube title and description and the caption for the other accounts, then Save words. What you save there is exactly what posts.
Approve to post sets it to post by itself on the card's day and time, to the accounts you chose, and each caption links back to your Halo post.
Seller updates (on AutoSparks, paid plans) send your weekly seller update by itself. In the Seller updates box, turn it On and pick the day and time, the video ( Avatar in circle or Email only ) and whether the sellers also get a text. Every listing with its sellers added from BoldTrail gets a card for that day (a listing without them shows Add sellers ). On the card, type the week's numbers (last week's show in grey; all optional) and what buyers said, then press Write it & make video, Email only, Record it myself · unlimited or Skip this week. When the video is done (about 5 to 10 minutes), Watch it, Preview email, and press Approve to send: it emails each seller through BoldTrail on its day, video included. Don't send it yourself from Spark Tools, or they get it twice. The Avatar in circle video uses 1 short video per listing each week; Email only uses none, and recording it yourself on camera is unlimited.
Don't post an approved video yourself from My Sparks or the Publish window. It posts by itself, so posting it by hand puts it up twice. The Publish window warns you when a video is set to post by itself. Already posted it yourself? Press Skip on the card instead of approving it.
After approving, you can still change Posts on until it's handed to your accounts. When to text Halo: after the video is published on your channel on its day and time, not before, because until then the link doesn't play. Then the card shows Put on my Halo post (it is on every Halo card, also for a video you posted yourself: paste its YouTube link in the box if it isn't filled in): it writes the message for you, and on your phone Text Halo opens your messages with it filled in, so Halo can add the video to the post. To put a video you posted yourself on your Halo post, text Halo at (415) 726-3224: “Halo, add this video to the top of my post [your post's link]: [your YouTube link]”. Skip sets a draft aside and its day is filled with the next new post.
Once Halo has added it, the card says ✓ On your Halo post and stops asking you to text Halo. SparkReels looks at your Halo post for the video each morning and when you open AutoSparks; if it hasn't noticed yet, press It's on my post (and Not yet undoes it). Finished cards (posted, and on your Halo post) fold into a Done line once newer cards arrive; Show opens them again.
Promo video for your Halo referral page
Add your Halo referral page too. It is marked Affiliate and has a Make promo video button. Pick an angle ( Why I use Halo, Free authority page or Halo Pro ) and press Write it. The script uses your referral code, and the video says out loud that you earn a referral fee when someone joins with it. The caption carries #ad for the same reason, as the law requires for paid referrals. It is set to post to Facebook, LinkedIn and Instagram, where other agents will see it. New script writes a fresh one. Promo videos are made when you ask, and are not one of your Halo videos for the month.
Email drafts
Every email you forward to your import address (step 6) also becomes a video draft in the same list, marked Email, about a minute after it arrives. It is set for the next free day at your Halo time and is not one of your Halo videos for the month. The script is written fresh from the email, so a market report from a data provider is never posted word for word. The email's photos are used for the thumbnail and, if you choose, on screen. Setup, Make video and Approve to post work the same as on a Halo draft. Up to 5 email drafts are written a day. Turn it off with the Forwarded emails switch in the Halo sites box; your emails still arrive in Spark Studio either way.

steps.title: Voice Over Only — The Scenes Reel
steps.text:
A Scenes Reel needs no photos, no camera and no face. Your voice clone reads the script over short, realistic scenes made with AI, one for each sentence, on screen while that sentence is spoken. It is the quickest video to make and a good fit for Reels and Shorts.
To make one: give the Topic card a topic, choose Video / Reel, pick Voice over only under it, and press Next. Or just say “make a reel about winter selling tips in Springfield”.
The script is written for you and waits to be read. Edit it, or tap Rewrite. Choose a length — 30 sec, 60 sec, 90 sec, 2 min or 3 min — Vertical or Horizontal, captions, music and your closing card, then press Build the Scenes reel.
It builds on its own after that, so you can leave the page. It shows as rendering in My Sparks and then as finished: a few minutes for a short one, around ten for three minutes. If it can't be built, My Sparks says so and nothing is taken from your plan.
The scenes show what each sentence is about and change from one to the next: close-ups, rooms, streets, different light. They are generic on purpose. People appear only from behind or at a distance, there are no readable words, and it is never your town or a real listing. For a real property use a Photos only reel with its own photos (step 19). A Scenes Reel uses one short video, and “Scenes made with AI.” is added to its description.

steps.title: Camera/Teleprompter — The Free Option
steps.text:
Pressing Camera/Teleprompter opens a page of its own, with Back on the bar at the bottom to return to Spark Studio. The mic box at the top holds what it's about; anything you already said or typed on Spark Studio comes with you. Then pick where the script comes from: AI writes it, From a document (a PDF, link or email), From a voice memo (a recording of you talking, turned into a clean script), Paste my own script (word for word), or No script (no teleprompter at all). Details are your market and, when AI or a document writes it, how long: up to 3, 8 or 15 minutes; More options holds audience, tone and why. Write my script in the bar at the bottom writes it, and Set up your take appears: your teleprompter, Behind you, vertical or horizontal, Branded Look, and Add Channel CTA to append your closing pitch. You can also skip straight here with Record on Camera, a one-click button on any script or blog post. The teleprompter scrolls automatically while you record in up to 1080p/60fps, for up to 15 minutes (8–15 min is YouTube's algorithm sweet spot and unlocks mid-roll ads). On a computer, press Record my screen under the script choices to record a listing, a market report or anything else on screen while you talk, with you in a corner circle or not. It records horizontal, up to 10 minutes, and finishes like any camera recording.
Read your script first in the script box, or press Read it full screen to see the whole script in large type and edit it there; Done takes you back. Under it, Flow follows your voice and keeps the line you're reading near the top, with the next lines below it. Auto scrolls at a steady speed you pick: Slow, Medium or Fast. While you record in Auto, tap − or + under the teleprompter to slow it down or speed it up without stopping. If Flow feels behind you, switch to Auto.
Behind you, in Set up your take, is what fills the screen while you talk in the corner: Just me (you, full screen), Your photos (up to 20), Your own footage, a video you shot that plays behind you (silent, and it loops), or AI scenes: short realistic scenes made with AI, one for each part of what you're about to say, in order. People appear only from behind or at a distance, and it is never your town or a real property. Scenes take about three minutes to make and use one short video from your plan; photos and your own footage stay free. Write the script first, because the scenes are made from it. Choosing a clip or scenes turns on Branded Look, which draws the background.
Smooth skin softens fine lines and blemishes while you record. With Branded Look on, pick Light or More in its box. The preview shows it right away, and your choice is remembered on that device.
With a clip or scenes chosen you can tick Open on it. The first 5 seconds of the take are then the clip full screen with a title you type, and you appear after that. Start talking as soon as you press record; your voice is heard over the opener.
Post a video you already shot — on a computer, open Camera/Teleprompter in Spark Studio and press Post a video as is under the script choices, then Choose a clip you already shot and pick a video from your computer: MP4, MOV or WebM, up to 2 minutes and 500 MB. Keep the clip's own sound or record a new voiceover, add a title, a hook and the city, then press Brand this clip. Your logo is added, captions are written from what's said, and the finished video is saved to My Sparks, ready to publish. It counts as a camera recording, not one of your plan's videos. This is on computers only; phones can't do the branding yet.
Don't want a take? Once it's saved, press Delete beside Re-record. It's removed from My Sparks, with its Share Kit, and you're back at the camera with your script ready.
If the upload doesn't go through, the take is kept on this device rather than lost. You'll see “Your recording is safely waiting on this device” with Retry Upload and Download. Retrying is always safe: it checks whether the recording already reached us rather than saving a second copy, so a lost reply can never turn into two videos. Download first if you want your own copy before leaving the page.

steps.title: Listings And Photos Only Reels
steps.text:
Listings & photos, the fourth card, opens a page of its own with two tabs, and both start from a set of property pictures. Back, on the bar at the bottom, returns to Spark Studio. Listing video writes a tour from the listing — paste a Zillow or Redfin link (other sites coming soon), upload photos or enter the details — and renders it in your voice, with your avatar on screen or the photos full-frame. It uses one short video. Once the address and price are in, press Next · video setup on the bar at the bottom to have the tour written, or Write it — I'll read it on camera to go straight to the teleprompter with your photos behind you, free.
A video takes up to 20 photos; Avatar video uses the first 15. When your photos are enough to fill the video, no stock footage is added.
Photos only reel needs no script at all. Add up to 12 photos — upload them, or paste a Zillow or Redfin link and its photos are brought in for you — then pick the format ( Vertical or Horizontal ), a length, music, and whether it has a voiceover and a closing card with your ask and phone number. A voiceover you type is read in your own voice clone once you have set one up, and by a stock voice until then. Then choose the Motion:
Classic is a slow pan across each photo. It is free and takes nothing from your plan.
Cinematic turns each photo into a few seconds of gentle camera movement, and uses one short video. It takes up to 8 photos and 60 seconds, and works best on rooms and exteriors — avoid photos with people in them, because they can come out looking different. Every clip is checked against its photo; one that drifts away from it is dropped and that photo gets the classic pan instead. If fewer than half your photos can be animated, no video is taken from your plan. “Photos animated with AI.” is added to the description, so the reel says what it is.
Open with me in front of the home (either kind, vertical or horizontal): your first photo becomes a 6-second shot of you at the front of the home, made with AI from your look. Choose Full body, Chest up or Off. It uses your Digital Twin once approved, otherwise your headshot.
Build the reel is on the bar at the bottom. When the reel is done it becomes View your reel. Make another reel, at the foot of the form, brings the build button back — on Cinematic that is another short video.
Post these photos, at the foot of the form, sends the same photos as they are: one post to swipe through on Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn, Threads, X or TikTok. No video is made and nothing comes out of your plan. Pick the accounts, write one caption for the post, and send. The order you arranged them in is the swipe order. Instagram takes the first ten, and trims a very tall or very wide photo to a shape it accepts.
No photos to start from? That is a Scenes Reel (step 17).

steps.title: Your Share Kit — And A Blog Post
steps.text:
Every video finishes on its Share Kit: the title, description and hashtags Publish fills in for you, plus an Instagram caption, a LinkedIn post and an email blurb. It also holds a blog article — usually 1,000 to 1,500 words, titled with the question a reader would actually type, headings written the same way and answered in the first line, and a Frequently Asked Questions section of six questions at the end, chosen from what people are asking about that subject in your town. Those six are AI answer blocks, built into every article (step 25). That is the shape an AI assistant quotes — AEO and GEO, alongside ordinary SEO. To change the words, press Edit on the article. The introduction, body and conclusion become boxes you can type in, with headings marked ##. Save keeps your changes, and Copy as HTML, the email version, the newsletter and BoldTrail all use them. The Headline box at the top of the article changes its title the same way. Header image makes the picture that sits above the headline — a real photograph of the kind of place the article is about, with no words drawn into it — and Copy as HTML then carries it across with the text, so what you paste into your site arrives with its image already in place. The same paste includes the article's schema, the hidden description that tells search and answer engines what the article is, who wrote it, and which parts are questions and answers. Some website builders remove it when you paste; the article is unaffected. Once an article has a header image, two more buttons appear beside it. Moving header turns that picture into a short silent loop of slow camera movement, and Copy as HTML then leads with it, keeping the still picture for sites that won't play video. Social teaser makes a short vertical clip with the headline and a “Read the full article” card, to download and post with a link. Each takes about a minute, neither uses a video from your plan, and each can be made up to four times for one article. That gives one recording two places to be quoted from: the video's own description, which is written with a real FAQ block for voice search, and the article on your own site. Blog posts never use a video from your plan, and you can write one without making a video at all — press the Blog card, which opens a page of its own with the mic box, Source and Details and Back on the bar at the bottom, or start your sentence with “create a blog”.
Posting it on your BoldTrail website. Press Copy as HTML. In BoldTrail, open your website (WebIDX), go to Blog and press Add Post. In the editor, click the <> button to open the code view, paste, and press Save. Give the post its title (use the Headline from your Share Kit), then Publish. Once it's live, open the post, copy its web address from your browser's address bar, and paste it into the email's link box, so Read more in your emails and newsletters goes straight to it.
Coming from a camera recording or a pasted script, the article starts writing itself as soon as the Share Kit opens — there is nothing to press. A take recorded with no script still has a Write the article button, because the words have to be taken off the video first. Before your free video it also waits for the button, so it never uses one of your free tries without being asked.
Email, in the article's row of buttons, turns the article into an email for your list: a short version with a button through to the full post. Paste in the address of the post on your site and the button points there. Send me a test sends it to the address you sign in with, so you can see it in a real inbox (look in spam the first time), and Copy as HTML drops it into the email tool you already use. With BoldTrail connected, Send through BoldTrail under the preview sends it to up to 10 people from your BoldTrail address, each greeted by their first name, once the post's web address is in. Without BoldTrail, SparkReels doesn't send it to your clients for you.
A newsletter from several posts. In My Sparks, press Make a newsletter above your Blog posts, tick 2 to 5 of them, then Make the newsletter. It writes three subject lines, the inbox preview, a short note from you, a few lines on each post with its own Read more button, and your sign-off. Paste each post's web address once; a post without one has no button. Copy as HTML drops it into the email tool you already use, and Send me a test sends it to you first. With BoldTrail connected, it can go to up to 10 people from there too, once every post's web address is in. Without BoldTrail, SparkReels doesn't send it to your clients for you.

steps.title: Publish To YouTube — One Click
steps.text:
Open the finished video in My Sparks and hit Publish. Your AI-generated title, description, and hashtags are attached automatically — choose public, unlisted, or private, and you're live without leaving the app. Avatar videos, Cinematic reels, Scenes reels and a camera recording made over AI scenes are marked to YouTube as AI-made when they go up, which YouTube asks for. Other videos you record yourself and Classic reels are not.
If a publish fails — an expired YouTube connection, a channel limit, a video still finishing — it isn't lost in a disappearing message. Open Publish on that video again: the top of the window lists where it has gone, and a failed one shows the reason with a Retry beside it. Once a later attempt goes through, the line reads as posted.
If YouTube needs reconnecting, which happens when Google ends the connection on its side, Publish says so and shows a Reconnect YouTube link. Your channel is remembered; reconnect and publish again.

steps.title: Everywhere Else — From The Same Window
steps.text:
The Publish window lists every account you connected in step 10. Tick the ones this video should go to and the button names them — Publish to Facebook, Publish to YouTube and Instagram. Nothing goes out until you press it. Creator posts each video to YouTube plus three others; Producer and Influencer post to all of them.
Caption / Post Text appears as soon as you tick anything besides YouTube. It starts with the caption and hashtags written for the video, and what you leave there is what gets posted.
First comment is optional, and is posted under the video on Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn, Threads and TikTok. It is the place for a link, because a link in an Instagram caption can't be clicked and one in a comment can. If you saved your blog post's address for this video, it is already filled in.
YouTube is live the moment it finishes. The others take a few minutes to process the video, so the window says On its way and tells you as each one lands, or why one did not. You can close it; the post carries on either way.
Where it's posted, at the top of the window, is the record for that video: one line for each platform, saying posted (with a link to the post), on its way, scheduled, or failed and why. A failed line has Retry, which sends the video to that one platform again. A posted line on Facebook or LinkedIn has Edit caption, for fixing the words after it is up; the other platforms don't allow that. Platforms the video is already on start unticked when you reopen the window, so it isn't posted to them twice by accident.
If a post doesn't go out after you've left the window, you are told two ways. A red note appears at the top of My Sparks naming the platform, the video and the reason, with Open Publish to go straight to Retry and Dismiss to clear it. And an email goes to the address you sign in with. The usual reason is a connection that has expired and needs connecting again in Settings; the note then has a Reconnect button.
Sparklee leaves short notes at the top of My Sparks too. Fixed for you says what went wrong and that she already fixed it, for example a missing avatar look swapped for another of yours, with nothing extra charged. Needs you is something only you can do, with the button for it. Dismiss either one with the ✕.
The thumbnail you set in the window is sent with the video as its cover, not only to YouTube. A vertical video gets a tall version of the same thumbnail. Each platform decides whether to show it; some pick a frame of their own.
Google Business works differently. It takes no more than 30 seconds of video and no phone numbers, so a longer video goes up as a photo post with your caption, any phone number left out, and a Learn more button to your blog post or the video. A long caption is trimmed to fit Google's limit. A video too long for one of the other platforms is skipped there, with the reason shown.
For an open house, tick Post to Google as an event and give it a name, the date and the start and end times. Google shows the date on your listing and takes the post down by itself afterwards, where an ordinary post would still say “this Saturday” a week later.
For anywhere you have not connected, download the MP4 and use the pre-written Instagram caption, LinkedIn post, and email blurb from the project's Title, Description & Hashtags card.
Email it. Any finished video in My Sparks can be emailed. Press Email it and add up to 10 people: search your BoldTrail by name or email (people you've sent a video to before, and your sellers, are one tap), or Add someone new with their name and email. Someone new is only saved to your BoldTrail if you tick Also add them to my BoldTrail. Without BoldTrail, type their first name and email. SparkReels writes a short subject and note that you can change or say out loud. Put {" "} in the note and each person sees their own name (a couple typed as “Jane and Tom” gets “Hi Jane and Tom”). The email shows your video's thumbnail, the one you edited, with a play button and a Watch the video button; email can't play a video inside the message, so a tap opens it. Send email asks you to confirm; tick Send me a copy to get one yourself, showing who it went to. BoldTrail contacts get it from your BoldTrail address; everyone else gets it from “your name via SparkReels”, with replies going to your own email (up to 30 a day). For your whole list, use your email tool or BoldTrail's own campaigns, which handle unsubscribes.

steps.title: The Everyday Tools
steps.text:
Spark Tools is in four groups: For a video (Thumbnail, Title, Description, Tags, Script, Record My Screen), Images & banners, Profile & reviews (Channel Name, LinkedIn Profile, Google Reviews, Ask for Google Review Video Email) and Sellers & AI search (Seller Update, AI Answer Blocks). Pick a group, then a tool. Record My Screen is the simple screen recorder: tick or untick Show me in a corner circle, press Start recording, pick the tab or window to show, talk as you go, and press Stop. Up to 10 minutes, free, saved to My Sparks with Watch, Download, Publish and Email it. Showing a web page? Open it in another tab first and pick that tab: the tab you record from is never offered, so the recording can't show itself. You don't need Spark Tools to make a video — Spark Studio generates everything automatically. Use these to iterate: brainstorm 8 title angles before committing, draft and compare scripts without creating projects, regenerate a description or 20 fresh tags for any video (including older ones), and name your channel (one-time). LinkedIn Profile is one-time too: it writes your headline, About, current position, top skills, custom URL and a post announcing your channel, each with where to paste it, and can write a Company Page for your team. From any project's Title, Description & Hashtags card, tap “Improve With AI Tools” and it opens the right tool with that project already loaded.
Google Reviews shows the reviews on your Google Business profile, with your average and how many there are. It needs Google Business connected (step 10). Needs a reply is ticked to begin with, so you see only the ones you haven't answered; untick it to see them all. On any review, Draft a reply writes a short one in your voice for you to edit, or Write my own gives you an empty box. Nothing goes to Google until you press Post reply. A reply you've already posted can be edited or removed. Read a drafted reply to a low rating with extra care before posting it. Ask for more reviews at the top opens the next tool.
Ask for Google Review Video Email sends past clients a short video asking for a review, with a big gold Leave me a Google review button under it. First save your link in Settings under Your Google review link (in your Google Business Profile: Ask for reviews → Copy link ). Then, in four steps: 1 Who: up to 10 people, picked from BoldTrail by name or email, or typed in by first name and email. 2 Your video: edit the words, then Record it myself (free, unlimited: the camera opens with the words on the teleprompter, and when it's saved, come back and it's picked for you), Avatar in circle (up to 60 seconds, uses 1 short video), Photo reel (upload your photos; the words show as text cards or your cloned voice reads them; free) or Use a video I made. 3 The email: the subject and note; {" "} becomes each person's first name. 4 Send email: BoldTrail contacts get it from your BoldTrail address. Someone new is saved to BoldTrail only if you tick Also add them to my BoldTrail; otherwise, and without BoldTrail, it comes from “your name via SparkReels” and replies go to your own email. That can land in Promotions or spam more often, so use Send me a test first. Tick Send me a copy when you send to get one yourself. The email shows your video's thumbnail with a play button.
Seller Update writes an update email to the people selling one of your listings, whenever you want to send one. Add the listing once: the address, the sellers' first names, the list price and the date it was listed. If you've already made a video or reel of it in Listings & photos, pick it under From your listings and the address fills in. For each update, fill in online views, saves, showings, open house visitors and offers, and type or say the buyer feedback and next steps. Your last update's numbers show beside each box, and the email shows the new ones as a row of numbers with what went up. It uses only what you enter. Past updates are listed under the listing. Record a video update writes a short script from your numbers and opens the camera with it; when you've recorded, Add to the seller update puts the video at the top of the email, where sellers tap it to watch. Your listings also sit under Seller updates in My Sparks, each with a New update button.
How to send a Seller Update Through BoldTrail: in the orange Sellers in BoldTrail box, start typing the seller's name or email and pick them from the list that drops down (or type the email exactly as it is in BoldTrail and press Add ). Their name shows as a chip (up to 4, once per listing). Only then does the orange Send to sellers through BoldTrail button appear, next to Copy as HTML. Press it and confirm; it emails each seller the update, video included, with an optional short text to say it's on its way. The update then shows when it was sent and to whom. The seller has to be a contact in BoldTrail already, and BoldTrail has to be connected in Settings.
Every week by itself: turn on Seller updates on AutoSparks (step 16). You add the numbers, watch the video and approve; it sends on its day.
From your own email: press Copy as HTML, paste it into a new email and send it. Copy as text is for a plain email or a text message.
Send me a test sends it to you first, so you see what your sellers will see.
The video in the preview on the right shows in a tall black box. That is only this screen's preview: in the email it is a small picture your sellers tap to watch.
Google Meet — Meet in the top bar on a computer, or in the menu on your phone. Start now opens a new Google Meet in a new tab; copy the link and send it to your client. Schedule for later asks for your client's name and email, the date, the time and how long, then opens Google Calendar with it all filled in: press Save, then Send to email them the invite. Calendar adds the Meet link; if none appears, click Add Google Meet video conferencing before saving. The meeting shows in Spark Calendar right away as a gold camera on its day; tap it to open that day in Google Calendar, or Remove it if you didn't save it in Google.

steps.title: Graphics Without A Designer
steps.text:
The Image Generator makes a finished graphic: pick Just listed, Open house, Market update, Blog header or Blank, describe the picture you want, and type your own headline. The photograph is generated; your words are drawn as real type on top, never by the AI — so a price or an address is always spelled right. Choose 4:5 for Instagram and Facebook, 9:16 for Stories and Reels, or 16:9 for a blog or YouTube, and it carries your logo and headshot.
Each press makes one AI photo and counts one against your monthly allowance of 100. Update text redraws your words on the same picture and costs nothing, and using My photo or one of your listing photos is free. New background makes another photo, and counts as one. Use as blog header sends it straight to the article it belongs to. Post it sends the finished graphic to your connected accounts as a photo post, with a caption you write, instead of downloading it first.
The Thumbnail Generator makes the cover picture for a video. Pick the video, type the few words you want on it or leave that blank and AI writes them, and choose the photo. Afterwards you can change the words or the photo and press Update Thumbnail, which redraws it in seconds on the same background. The Market Badge is the city and state shown on it. Type a different one to change it, which also updates the video's market so its title and description match, or clear both boxes and press Update Thumbnail to leave the badge off.
Banners makes the wide image across the top of your YouTube channel, your LinkedIn profile or your Facebook page, each at the size that site wants. For YouTube, press Use this template and your photo, logo, name and contact details fill in from Settings. Change any of it, and everything stays inside the part every phone and TV shows. The LinkedIn and Facebook banners let you put your photo on the left or the right and add QR codes to your site. Pick a color palette or choose Custom and set your own colors. Download the picture, or use Download for Canva (PDF) for a copy meant to be opened in Canva, where you can change the text and colors yourself.

steps.title: AI Answer Blocks — Get Cited By AI Search
steps.text:
Buyers ask ChatGPT and Perplexity things like “which neighborhood should I buy in?” months before they call an agent. On Create, under the topic box, What buyers ask AI shows a question buyers in your city are asking right now, using the city in Settings unless you type another in Details. Show more opens the rest, and Record this makes one your topic, so the video answers it.
Every blog article already has answer blocks. The six questions at the end of each article in your Share Kit (step 20) are written the way AI assistants quote, for that article's topic, so there is nothing extra to make.
The full tool is in Spark Tools, under Sellers & AI search. For each question it also gives a ready-to-paste block for your website and a Record on Camera shortcut straight to the teleprompter.

steps.title: What A Spark Is
steps.text:
A Spark is one idea and everything that came out of it: the script, the video or videos made from it, the article, the captions, and where each has been published. One topic, one Spark — even if you make a short version, a long version and a reel from it.
Two places in the menu use the word, and they hold different things. My Sparks is your library: the finished videos and drafts themselves, to watch, download, publish or delete. To delete several at once, press Select on the Videos or Blog posts heading, tick them, and press Delete. The All Sparks panel inside Spark Calendar lists the Sparks — open one and you get its card, holding the article, the captions, the schedule and how it's performing.

steps.title: Spark Insights — What You Have And How It Did
steps.text:
Spark Insights opens with what you have left — short videos, long videos, and whether camera recording is unlocked with the days remaining — a Getting Started checklist that disappears once you've finished it, and buttons to create a video or open the calendar. Your five most recent projects are at the bottom to pick back up.
Then it looks backwards. How many videos you've made and published, a breakdown by platform and by video shape, and — for anything published to your connected YouTube channel — real views, likes and comments, with every video ranked and linked. Those numbers are fetched from YouTube once a day, so they're yesterday's picture rather than live, and they only cover videos published from September onwards. The same figures appear on each Spark's own card, counting just that Spark's videos.
Watch time and click-through aren't there yet — YouTube keeps those behind a separate permission. Views, likes and comments are what a connected channel gives us today.

steps.title: Spark Calendar — When It Goes Out
steps.text: The calendar puts every dated item — published or scheduled — on a month, week or list view, with the All Sparks panel beside it for everything that has no date yet. Open any Spark from either side to reach its card. This one is still rolling out: it appears in your menu when your account has it.

steps.title: Earn With The Affiliate Program
steps.text:
Recommend SparkReels and earn 20% of what each customer you refer pays, every month for their first 12 months. The SparkReels Affiliate Program is available to active paid subscribers. Open Affiliate in the menu and press Apply to join, or sign in and use Affiliates at the bottom of the website, and tell us a little about how you'd share SparkReels. If your plan ends, your affiliate account is paused: earnings you already have are kept and paid when you subscribe again, but payments your referrals make while you're paused don't earn a commission. When you're approved, you'll get an email titled “You're approved — welcome to the SparkReels affiliate program” with your referral code, your referral link and two steps. First, open the link in it while signed in, to connect the program to your account. Then, on the Affiliate page, connect your bank with Stripe to get paid. Payouts are sent monthly. If the email hasn't arrived, look in spam.
Also a Halo affiliate? On the Affiliate page, put your Halo page (like halo-your-name.huzi.site ) or your Halo code in Your Halo affiliate link and press Save. Agents you refer to SparkReels then get your link on their Get Halo button. With only a code, the button texts “CODE PRO” to Halo instead. Under it, Pressed Get Halo lists each agent who pressed it, with their name, email and date, so you can find them on your Halo dashboard and see who signed up.

parts.title: Getting Around
parts.text:
The menu runs across the top on a computer: Spark Studio, My Sparks, AutoSparks, Spark Tools, Spark Calendar, Spark Insights, Affiliate, Settings, What's New and How It Works. What's New shows the latest features, with a gold dot when there is one you haven't seen; each has Learn How It Works, which brings you to its step here. The page you are on is underlined. On a smaller window the last few are under More; on a phone, tap ☰.
Settings has three tabs. Profile holds your brand, market, voice, closing call to action, import address and password. Social Accounts is where YouTube and your other platforms are connected. Billing is your plan and buying more videos. At the top of Profile, Your studio: 6 of 8 ready lists the eight things that make your videos look and sound like you; each one still to do has a button that takes you to it.
Your initial, at the top right, opens your email, your plan and Sign Out.
Sparklee, the gold star beside it, answers out loud when you ask how to do something on the page you are on. Tap her to start, and tap Stop when you're done.
Put SparkReels on your phone's Home Screen so it opens like an app. On an iPhone, open sparkreels.ai in Safari, tap the Share button (the square with an arrow), then Add to Home Screen. On Android, open it in Chrome, tap the ⋮ menu, then Add to Home screen (or Install app ).
The first time you sign in, Sparklee asks you to set up your profile. Ask me how has her talk you through it; Go to Settings takes you straight there.
Part 1 · One-Time Setup

parts.title: Ways To Create
parts.text:
Mode | Best For | Cost
Camera/Teleprompter | Film yourself with the teleprompter | FREE, unlimited*
Blog | Words for your own site — no video made at all | FREE, unlimited*
Avatar video | You on screen, with b-roll and graphics made for you. Up to 2 minutes | 1 short video
Avatar in circle | You in a corner circle, over AI scenes that follow each sentence, with your photos among them | 1 short video
Voice over only | A Scenes Reel: no face, no photos, no camera. Your voice over AI scenes, up to 3 minutes | 1 short video
My Content/Forwarded in | A finished script spoken exactly as written — or an article, a PDF, a link or a forwarded email that AI writes from | FREE as a blog*
1 short video as a video
Listing video | A scripted tour, written from the listing | 1 short video
Photos only reel · Classic | Your photos with a slow pan across each, and music or your voice | FREE
Photos only reel · Cinematic | Each photo becomes a few seconds of real camera movement | 1 short video
* Unlimited on any paid plan. On the free 100-agent beta, camera recording, blog posts and every AI Tool are unlimited for 14 days starting the day you generate your free video. Before that video, you get 1 free blog, 1 free camera recording, 2 free tries of the AI Tools and 2 free AI images to see how they work — one try per tool run. Making the video is free and lifts all of those limits.

parts.title: Get It In Front Of People
The Weekly Rhythm
parts.text:
Once: set up your profile, voice, avatar, CTA, YouTube and your email import address (Part 1)
Weekly: hit the mic and say it, tap a topic chip, or forward a report → generate script → Spark Video — about 5 minutes of your time
Hands off: add your Halo site on AutoSparks, or forward an email, and approve the drafts that show up there — they make and post themselves
Publish: one window sends it to YouTube and the other accounts you connected, with title, description, and tags attached
For a listing: a Classic photos only reel is free; Cinematic or a listing video uses one short video
No photos and no camera: Voice over only makes a Scenes Reel from a topic, up to 3 minutes, for one short video
Mix in free camera videos — YouTube's algorithm loves 8–15 minute authentic long-form
